kurz: Coffee and tea are extraction: hot water dissolves aromas from beans or leaves. Roast, grind size, temperature and time decide what comes out.
bild_im_kopf: Like a teabag and patience: too short tastes thin, too long bitter.
was_passiert: During roasting, the aromas form through the [[maillard-reaktion|Maillard reaction]] and [[karamellisierung|caramelisation]]. When brewing, acids and fruity aromas dissolve first, then sweetness, and finally bitter compounds.
warum_wichtig: Sour coffee is usually extracted too briefly or too coarsely; bitter coffee too long or too finely.
faustregeln: Sour: grind finer or brew longer.
Bitter: grind coarser or brew shorter.
Green tea at about 70–80 °C, not boiling (as a guide).
